title: Is this even enough data?
brief:
A team has plotted its first **six weeks** of theatre start-time delays (minutes) and is keen to declare that things are improving. The median is the dashed line.

Before reading any signal, ask the prior question: is there enough data?

task.stem: Can you reliably apply the run-chart rules to this chart yet?

options.label: Yes — six points is plenty to call a signal.
No — you generally need about 10–12 points or more before the rules are reliable; keep collecting.
Yes, but only the astronomical-point rule works with few points.
No — you need exactly 30 points before any run chart can be read.

debrief.correct: Right. With only six points, the run-chart rules are not yet reliable — you generally want **about 10–12 points or more** before a shift, trend, or runs signal means much. Six points can look like an improvement purely by chance. Keep collecting data on the same measure, keep the median provisional, and re-read the chart as it grows. Declaring victory now risks acting on noise.
debrief.wrong: The run-chart rules need enough data to work: **roughly 10–12 points or more**. Six points is too few — a short downward wiggle can happen by chance and is not a signal. It is not that only one rule works, and there is no magic '30 points' threshold; you simply keep collecting until the chart is long enough to read.
debrief.rule_cited: Minimum data for run-chart interpretation — Provost & Murray (2nd ed.); Perla, Provost & Murray on run-chart rules.
